## Milestone 1 - Task 5.1: Excel Writer

Consumes the Report Contract produced by 06-documentation-agent (docs/contracts/report-contract.md) and updates one row of an existing QA Excel workbook. A pure renderer: it never inspects a Decision Contract directly, never calls AI, never judges pass/fail, and never modifies the Report Contract it receives - it only reads from it.

Updates renderer-owned columns only (Status, Actual Result, Notes, Tester Notes, Confidence, Decision Basis, Manual Review, Execution Date, Evidence Summary). Test ID, Description, Steps, and Expected Result - the original test definition - are never written by this workflow; they are preserved by construction (see 'Locate & Merge Row').

No new field is added to the Report Contract and no change is made to 06-documentation-agent.json - this workflow only reads what that contract already provides.

## Renderer architecture (Task 5.1)

Every renderer - this one and every future one (Google Sheets, PDF, dashboards) - follows the same four-stage shape, so the Report Contract never has to know which renderer is reading it:

```
Report Contract
      |
      v
Renderer Adapter   <- 'Excel Adapter' below: Report Contract fields
      |                 only, renderer-agnostic canonical names
      v
COLUMN_MAP         <- 'Apply Column Map' below: canonical names
      |                 -> this renderer's real column headers
      v
Renderer           <- everything from 'Read Workbook File' on:
                        xlsx-specific, owns the actual write
```

A future Sheets Adapter would produce the exact same canonical field object 'Excel Adapter' does (both derive from the same Report Contract fields) - only 'Apply Column Map' (target column headers) and everything after it (xlsx vs Sheets API) would differ. Building a second renderer never requires touching 06-documentation-agent.json or docs/contracts/report-contract.md.

## Design notes

- REPORT_FILE_PATH ('/data/reports/qa-report.xlsx') is a fixed literal, defined identically in 'Read Workbook File' and 'Write Workbook File' (n8n Code nodes can't share constants with native nodes' parameters - same manual-sync convention docs/workflow-standards.md already accepts for COLUMN_MAP/AGENT_ROUTES). Never derived from item data, so there is no path-traversal surface from a malformed Report Contract.
- Read-modify-write, not append: every row from the existing workbook is read, exactly one row is updated in place, and the full row set (unchanged rows included) is written back - this is what keeps every other test's row, and every non-renderer-owned column on the target row, byte-for-byte untouched.
- Idempotent by construction: re-running with the same Report Contract locates the same row and overlays the same 9 values again - no new row is ever appended, and a converged value stays converged.
- No retry logic on 'Read Workbook File' / 'Write Workbook File' failures - same 'no retry, no classification' convention as every prior workflow's native-node error handling (e.g. 05's 'Claude' -> 'Build AI Service Error').
